label: Differentiable Manifolds: The Toolkit
notes: This appendix, printed pages 209 through 213, gathers the smooth-manifold background the book leans on. We preview the chain: topological manifold, atlas of charts, smooth structure, then tangent spaces and quotients. Each item is a tool the later manifold statistics quietly assume, so this review makes those assumptions explicit before we infer on shapes.

label: Topological Manifolds
notes: A topological manifold looks locally like Euclidean space of fixed dimension, while staying Hausdorff and second countable so analysis behaves. These mild global conditions rule out pathologies and guarantee partitions of unity, which we need to glue local statistics into a single global estimator on the manifold later in the text.

label: Charts and the Atlas
notes: A chart is a homeomorphism from an open set of the manifold to an open set of Euclidean space, giving local coordinates. An atlas is a collection of charts covering the manifold. Charts are the working coordinates in which we actually compute means, projections, and densities throughout the inference chapters.

label: Transition Maps and Smooth Structure
notes: Where two charts overlap, the composition of one inverse with the other is a transition map between Euclidean open sets. Requiring every transition map to be infinitely differentiable defines the smooth, or C-infinity, structure. This compatibility is exactly what lets us call a coordinate-free quantity well defined rather than chart dependent.

label: Smooth Maps and Diffeomorphisms
notes: A map between manifolds is smooth when it is smooth read through any compatible charts. A diffeomorphism is a smooth bijection with smooth inverse, the right notion of equivalence for smooth manifolds. Diffeomorphism invariance is why estimators built intrinsically do not depend on an arbitrary choice of coordinates.

label: Immersions and Embeddings
notes: An immersion has an injective differential at every point; an embedding is an injective immersion that is also a homeomorphism onto its image. The Whitney embedding theorem says every smooth manifold embeds in some Euclidean space, which justifies the extrinsic, ambient-space analysis the book often uses for shapes.

label: The Tangent Space
notes: The tangent space at a point collects velocity vectors of smooth curves through that point, equivalently the derivations of germs of smooth functions. It is a vector space of the same dimension as the manifold and is the linear stage where tangent-space statistics, covariances, and confidence regions are computed in the main text.

label: The Differential and Pushforward
notes: A smooth map induces a linear differential, the pushforward, sending tangent vectors to tangent vectors by acting on curve velocities. It is the coordinate-free derivative whose rank classifies immersions and submersions. Pushforwards transport tangent-space uncertainty along maps, the precise mechanism behind the delta method on manifolds.

label: Submanifolds and Regular Values
notes: A regular value of a smooth map is one whose every preimage point has surjective differential. The regular value theorem then makes the preimage a smooth submanifold of predictable dimension. This is the standard machine for certifying that constraint sets, like spheres and matrix groups, are genuine smooth manifolds we can do statistics on.

label: Orientation
notes: An orientation is a consistent, smoothly varying choice of basis ordering across charts, possible only when transition Jacobians keep positive determinant. Orientability lets us integrate top-degree forms and define signed volume, which underlies volume measures and densities used when defining intrinsic means and nonparametric estimators on the manifold.

label: Quotient Manifolds and Group Actions
notes: When a Lie group acts smoothly, freely, and properly on a manifold, the orbit space inherits a unique smooth quotient structure. Free and proper together prevent collapsing and tangled orbits. This is the exact mechanism producing shape spaces: quotient configurations by similarity or rotation to obtain the smooth manifold on which we infer.

label: Recap: From Charts to Shape Spaces
notes: We assembled the appendix toolkit: charts and a smooth atlas, smooth maps and diffeomorphisms, immersions and Whitney embedding, tangent spaces and pushforwards, the regular value theorem, orientation, and proper free quotients. Together they license the coordinate-free, embedding-based, and quotient constructions that the rest of the book uses to do statistics on shapes.
